questions.q: What are the two kinds of spherical mirrors?
questions.a: Concave (inner curved surface reflects) and convex (outer surface reflects).

questions.q: Which mirror is used as a dentist's mirror and why?
questions.a: Concave - it gives an enlarged, upright image of the tooth when close.

questions.q: Which mirror is used in vehicle rear-views and why?
questions.a: Convex - it gives a wide, upright view of traffic behind.

questions.q: What kind of image does a concave mirror form when the object is far away?
questions.a: A small, inverted, real image in front of the mirror.

questions.q: What image does a convex mirror always form?
questions.a: A small, upright (virtual) image, whatever the object's position.
One where rays actually meet and can be caught on a screen, like cinema images.

questions.q: State the two laws of reflection.
questions.a: Angle of incidence equals angle of reflection, and the rays and normal lie in one plane.

questions.q: What is the normal in reflection?
questions.a: The perpendicular line to the mirror surface at the point where the ray strikes.

questions.q: Which surface reflects light regularly - mirror or wall? Why?
questions.a: A mirror - its smooth surface sends parallel rays back parallel; a wall scatters them.

questions.q: How does a convex lens differ from a concave lens?
questions.a: A convex lens is thicker in the middle and converges light; a concave lens is thinner in the middle and diverges it.

questions.q: Which lens is used to correct short-sightedness?
Give one use of a convex lens.
questions.a: Magnifying glass, camera, or eye lens - it forms images of objects.
